title: The 10 Best Biscuit Joiners
subtitle: Corded and cordless biscuit (plate) joiners for tabletops, cabinets and frames, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A biscuit joiner cuts slots for glued wooden biscuits that align and strengthen joints in tabletops, cabinets and frames. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Makita, PORTER-CABLE, WEN and budget brands on rating, review volume and features (a rack-and-pinion fence, an angle fence, dust collection, cordless power and biscuits in the box).

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

avoid.name: Ecarke Cordless Biscuit Joiner Compatible with DeWalt 20V Battery
avoid.verdict: A DEWALT-battery joiner with a fixed fence, which makes centering slots on boards of different thickness harder, and the lowest rating of the joiners we looked at.
reasons: The listing describes a 'sturdy fixed baffle' and an 'auxiliary module' to change the blade offset, rather than a fence you can raise and lower; the joiners we rank adjust height on a fence or rack-and-pinion.
It's rated 3.6 stars on 42 reviews, the lowest of the joiners we looked at.
DEWALT owners can buy the DCW682B, which uses the same batteries with a dual rack-and-pinion fence and 4.8 stars.

buyers_guide.q: What does a biscuit joiner do?
buyers_guide.a: It cuts matching crescent slots in two boards. You glue in a compressed wooden biscuit, which swells and locks the joint and keeps edges aligned. It's fast for tabletops, cabinet carcasses and face frames.
#0, #10 and #20 cover most work; use the largest that fits the board. Most joiners have preset stops for all three.
The fence sets how far the slot is from the face. A rack-and-pinion fence stays parallel to the blade, so slots line up on both boards. A tilting fence handles mitered corners.
Corded is cheaper and has unlimited runtime. Cordless DEWALT and Makita joiners are handy for site work and assembly in place.
Biscuits are quickest and forgiving for alignment. Dowels and Festool Domino tenons are stronger for chairs and frames under heavy load.
